items.title: No weekly baseline of comment quality
items.whyItMatters: One review of 200 forms cannot separate a later rise from ordinary variation.
items.opportunity: Rate 25 comments a week from August and September forms to give eight baseline points before cycle 1.

items.title: Effects fade without reinforcement
items.whyItMatters: Teaching alone lost most of its effect by six months (claim c3).
items.opportunity: Add monthly individual reports in cycle 3 and track whether faculty open them.

items.title: Raters can see which period a comment comes from
items.whyItMatters: Chief residents who expect improvement may rate borderline comments leniently.
items.opportunity: Rate comment text only, pasted without dates or form layout, in mixed batches, with 20 percent double-rated.

items.title: Comment quality may differ by resident gender
items.whyItMatters: Women residents received non-actionable comments more often elsewhere (claim c4).
items.opportunity: Plot the outcome separately by resident gender each month.

items.title: Longer prompts could reduce or delay forms
items.whyItMatters: Fewer or later forms would trade quantity and timeliness for quality.
items.opportunity: Track forms completed per week and days from encounter to completion as balancing measures.

errorsFound: The need counts forms with any comment as feedback given; the retrieved evidence shows most such comments are generic and unused by residents.
reevaluation: The gaps support a measurement-first QI project with a blinded-as-possible weekly rating, a three-part change package with reinforcement, balancing measures and a gender breakdown.
summary: Five gaps: no baseline, fading effects, rater bias, possible gender inequity and quantity or timeliness trade-offs.
